ip.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
ip.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

ip.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
ip.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

ip.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
ip.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers. zh CORRECTED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 QA): the wave-2 zh translating agent initially deviated to the generic academic term '灌水器' throughout ip_ keys, reasoning that the calculator's emitter-exponent model (x from ~0 to 0.5) is generic rather than drip-only. Reverted to the established glossary field term '滴头' (dripper) for suite-wide consistency with the ar/es/uk pattern above — this glossary's own policy is field-term-over-academic-generality across all languages, and a generic hydraulic model doesn't change what practitioners actually call the part.

ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file). Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): tr confirmed on dağılım düzgünlüğü — transliteration+wrong-word forms Uniformluk/Dağıtım were corrected across 7 keys.

ip.context: Irrigation statistic: average of the lowest quarter of measured emitter flows divided by the overall average. Referenced in Irrigation Pressure notes as "textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity".
ip.translation_notes: Use the established irrigation-engineering phrase; do not invent one. "Textbook" is an adjective meaning "as defined in standard textbooks" — fr rendered it "manuel" (manual check), wrong. he: uniformity = אחידות, never the nonword הוודות. Wave-1 coinages (2026-07, category-4 sprint): fr="uniformité de distribution du quart inférieur", ro="Uniformitatea Distribuției de sfert inferior", ru="равномерность распределения по нижней четверти", uk="рівномірність розподілу по низькій чверті", bg="равномерност на разпределение по долната четвърт", sr="равномерност расподеле нижег квартила", hr="jednolikost distribucije niske grupe", cs="Uniformita distribuce nízké čtvrtiny", tr="düşük-çeyrek Dağıtım Uniformluğu", id="Keseragaman Distribusi kuartal-bawah". es/pt/it/de already had glossary coverage pre-sprint. Not yet native-reviewed. ur ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 sprint): "نچلی چوتھائی تقسیم یکسانیت" (lower-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the established ur terms چوتھائی (quarter), تقسیم (distribution), یکسانیت (uniformity, already glossary term for plain "distribution uniformity"). Not yet native-reviewed. hi ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'निम्न-चतुर्थांश वितरण एकरूपता' (low-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the glossary's own hi="वितरण एकरूपता" for the base "distribution uniformity" term and prefixes "निम्न-चतुर्थांश" (low-quarter), matching the wave-1 pattern of naming the concept literally (fr/ru/uk/id etc.) rather than inventing a new metaphor. Where the English source's own qualifier 'standard' appears in context (ip_du_estimate, ip_notes_3_def), it is rendered inline as 'القياسي' immediately after this base phrase, kept out of the pure glossary term here for parity with the other languages' entries. bn ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'নিম্ন-চতুর্থাংশ বিতরণ সমতা' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own bn="বিতরণ সমতা" base term, naming the concept literally. fa ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'یکنواختی توزیع ربع پایین' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own fa="یکنواختی توزیع" base term; where English says "standard" it is rendered inline as "استاندارد" immediately after this base phrase, same pattern as ar. Task 129 STALE-ENGLISH RESYNC (2026-07-21): the ip_ keys ip_du_estimate/ip_q_ratio/ip_notes_3_def (plus ip_worst_case_warn and mhp_notes_2_def) were resynced against the CURRENT English, which was shortened in the Wave-0 reform (commit 7bfbda1) after several languages had already translated the older, longer version. ip.preferred_translation: uniformidade de distribuição do quarto inferior

ip.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation. Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): hi 'सिंचाई दर' (irrigation rate) drift standardized to file-dominant अनुप्रयोग term (ip_pr='अनुप्रयोग दर'); am confirmed on ልፍፍ.

ip.context: Irrigation branch line carrying emitters, fed by the mainline. Pairs with "mainline". Appears throughout Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: Branch pipe of a drip/sprinkler system — NOT the adjective "side/lateral". Wrong renderings found: sw "taji" (crown). fr irrigation standard is "rampe". Keep one word per language and never alternate (it file mixed "laterale" and "manichetta").

ip.context: The trunk/supply pipe feeding the laterals in an irrigation system. Pairs with "lateral".
ip.translation_notes: Translate "main/mainline" as the trunk pipe, not the adjective "main". fr file left "main" untranslated ("Tronçons Main") — wrong.

ip.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
ip.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong). Bisection is the numerical root-finding method used to close the pressure loop in the Irrigation Pressure notes. (Wave 0, 2026-07-07, removed the former "right at the takeoff" and "draw off" wording from the English source.) Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): confirmed the single suite term per language — ar=قطاع (harmonized from a مقطع/قطاع split, مقطع left meaning cross-section) and ur=حصہ (harmonized from پہنچ in cs_ vs transliterated ریچ in ip_).

ip.context: Kinetic energy per unit weight, V²/2g — a height of water column.
ip.translation_notes: "Head" is a height of water column, never anatomical (cs "rychlostní hlava" wrong — use "rychlostní výška"). Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): confirmed he=עומד מהירות (literal ראש 'head' calque removed) and sw=kimo cha kasi (Kichwa cha kasi calque removed).

ip.context: Head loss along the pipe due to wall friction (Darcy-Weisbach). Symbol h_f (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per label-normalization decision item 90, 2026-07-07). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure table column.
ip.translation_notes: Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am 'ፍሪክሽን ኪሳራ' transliteration corrected to 'ግጭት ኪሳራ' (matches shipped mphl_friction_loss); same 'friction' fix applied across 5 keys.

ip.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de 'Minderverlust' (=lesser/reduced loss — the exact 'smaller loss' mistranslation the item-90 convention blocks) corrected to 'Örtlicher (Einzel-)Verlust' matching the labels.

ip.context: The total-head line (elevation + pressure head + velocity head) along a pipe or channel. Appears in Irrigation Pressure Method note.
ip.translation_notes: Use the established hydraulics term for the total-head line. NEVER calque word-by-word: es "Linea de Grado de Energia", fr "ligne d'energie grade", it "Linea di Grado Energia", ro "Linia Gradului Energetic", bg/uk "line of the energy class", cs "energy layer" are all wrong renderings found in shipped files. Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

ip.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
ip.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

mhp.context: Pressure pipe carrying water from a reservoir or headpond down to a turbine in a micro-hydro system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Penstock' is a specialized term with no exact one-word equivalent in many languages. Use the established civil/hydro engineering phrase for 'pressure conduit' or 'force main to turbine'. Czech: 'tlakovod' (pressure main) is preferred over the generic 'přiváděcí potrubí' (supply pipe). Serbian: 'напорни цевовод' is the standard hydraulic engineering term. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. 2026-07-13 Task 103 follow-up: am/bn/ru values below were themselves stale phonetic transliterations of the English word (same defect class as the earlier 'riprap' audit) — corrected to compositional 'pressure pipe' phrases matching the shipped, agent-fixed lang files. When English 'penstock' itself reads as jargon, pair the primary term with a plain '(supply pipe)' gloss in the UI rather than leaving it unglossed — see mhp_diameter tooltip pattern. Task 130 (2026-07-21): the (supply pipe) gloss was applied to mhp_diameter in the 15 languages that lacked the tooltip; each language reused its existing penstock term (no term changes, wrapper+gloss only).

mhp.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

mhp.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

mhp.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. Use the energy/electrical engineering term for overall system efficiency. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

mhp.context: A hydropower configuration that uses natural river flow without a dam or significant storage reservoir. Power output varies with seasonal river flow. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: Use the established energy/hydropower sector term. 'Run' means natural river current — do not translate as jogging or running. WMO No. 385 entry 1263 gives the full facility names: Spanish 'central hidroeléctrica de pasada', French 'usine hydroélectrique au fil de l'eau', Russian 'русловая гидроэлектростанция' — these are the authoritative terms for the power plant noun. The abbreviated forms 'filo de agua' (es), 'au fil de l'eau' (fr), and 'русловая ГЭС' (ru) are standard in engineering use. German: 'Laufwasserkraftwerk'. Chinese: '径流式水电'. Task 98 audit (2026-07-13): 'micro-hydro' (the companion term this concept pairs with in mhp_ keys) had been left completely untranslated/transliterated in 4 languages, not just run-of-river — sw and km kept the raw Latin 'Micro-Hydro' embedded in otherwise-native sentences; km and ps also left 'Run-of-River' in an English parenthetical even where the surrounding sentence already translated the concept; ps separately phonetically transliterated 'مایکرو هایدرو' as its own word throughout (same defect, different script). All 4 fixed: sw → 'Umeme Mdogo wa Maji' (small electricity of water), km → 'ថាមពលវារីអគ្គិសនីខ្នាតតូច' (small-scale hydroelectric power, reusing km's own native hydro vocabulary), ps → 'کوچنی آبي ځواک' (small water-power, real Pashto not transliteration) with the redundant English '(Run-of-River)' parenthetical dropped in both km and ps since their own sentences already conveyed it. ar ('الطاقة الكهرومائية الصغيرة') and zh ('微型水力发电') were already clean and served as the quality reference for the fixes.

mhp.context: The intake structure at the upstream end of a penstock or canal, where water is diverted from the river or reservoir into the conveyance system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator (penstock diameter and length descriptions).
mhp.translation_notes: Use the civil/irrigation engineering term for a water intake or diversion structure. Spanish: 'obra de toma'. French: 'ouvrage de prise d'eau'. Russian: 'водозаборное сооружение'. German: 'Einlaufbauwerk'. In many languages, 'intake structure' is preferred over a literal translation of 'headworks'.

mhp.context: Energy loss at pipe junctions, bends, fittings, and entrance — a local (point) loss as opposed to distributed friction loss along the pipe. h_m = k_m × v²/(2g). Appears in Manning Pipe Head Loss and Micro-Hydro Power calculators.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07): the suite-wide English label for this concept is "Minor (local) loss" — 'junction loss' (formerly mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_) are merged into it; see the 'minor loss' entry for the canonical treatment. The term 'minor' is conventional but misleading — do not imply these losses are always small; the parenthetical '(local)' carries the true sense. Use the hydraulic engineering term for local/point losses at fittings. French: 'perte singulière'. Spanish: 'pérdida local' or 'pérdida por accesorio'. Russian: 'местные потери'. Chinese: '局部水头损失'. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de mphl_total_junction_k_tip aligned to örtlich/'(local)' label wording; hi/id/ur had the 'minor (local)' word order reversed against their own labels and were corrected.

mhp.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de 'Minderverlust' (=lesser/reduced loss — the exact 'smaller loss' mistranslation the item-90 convention blocks) corrected to 'Örtlicher (Einzel-)Verlust' matching the labels.

mtc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
mtc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

mtc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

mtc.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): previous sw value 'radius ya maji' (literally 'radius of water', English loanword 'radius' + 'of water') named the substance rather than the hydraulic-geometry property, and did not read as an engineering term. Changed to 'radiasi ya kihaidroliki' (radius + 'hydraulic', adjectival ki- form), matching the '[radius] + hydraulic' construction used by fr/de/it/es/ro/tr (rayon hydraulique / hydraulischer Radius / raggio idraulico / radio hidráulico / raza hidraulică / hidrolik yarıçap). Used in lib/lang.ec.sw.php's mpf_hydraulic_radius.

mtc.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use. Task 109 stages 4 & 5 (2026-07-19): bg wrong-word 'навлажнен' (moistened) corrected to 'омокрен' in mpf_wetted_perimeter (stage 4) and cs_notes_3_def (stage 5); km គ្រែទឹក (water bed) also confirmed corrected to glossary បរិវេណសើម (stage 4).

mtc.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mtc.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'. mtc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.
